A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dolphin research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-separation experiments, visual reconstruction results, efficiency measurements, and architectural ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a VQ-removal experiment, acoustic robustness tests, and a human listening study.

M1.justification: The proposed DP-LipCoder, fusion module, GLA separator, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Section 3.2 newly clarifies that the encoder paths do not share parameters; VQ removal is an experimental control, not a revision of the proposed model.

E1.justification: The original datasets and multi-speaker tasks remain. v2 Appendix I adds VoxCeleb2 scenarios combining FSD50K environmental noise or FMA music with one or three speakers. Appendix J adds naturally overlapping speech from debate recordings, substantially extending evaluation beyond artificially constructed speech mixtures.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 introduces a VQ-free DP-LipCoder control, distinct from the earlier AE and LipCoder comparators. External baseline membership in matched comparisons is unchanged; the added noise and listening evaluations reuse IIANet and AV-Mossformer2.

E3.justification: New protocols include controlled retraining without VQ, 1,000 test samples per noise scenario, and a randomized, double-blind five-point MOS study with 50 listeners rating 18 clips lasting 10–20 seconds. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; Table 2's added retraining description is a disclosure rather than evidence of a revised protocol.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix G directly tests VQ's contribution by removing the quantizer and commitment loss while retaining reconstruction and distillation objectives. Appendix I adds systematic environmental-noise, music, and interfering-speaker robustness tests. Earlier component, iteration, depth, output-formulation, and fusion-location ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 10 introduces MOS averages with ± values, whereas v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. The PDF does not define whether these values represent standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals. No additional training-run or seed reporting is provided.

E6.justification: Retained tables preserve their scores. New Table 7 reports SI-SNRi of 16.3 without VQ versus 16.8 with VQ. Table 9 adds four noisy-scenario comparisons, with Dolphin leading all reported metrics. Table 10 reports MOS of 3.86 ± 0.25 for Dolphin, 2.24 ± 0.15 for IIANet, and 2.85 ± 0.27 for AV-Mossformer2. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The DCT/heat-diffusion formulation and equations 1–28, including the appendix architecture and loss definitions, are retained. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and main conclusion retain the same contributions: discrete dual-path visual encoding, a single-iteration GLA separator, and improved separation–efficiency trade-offs. The new experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning synchronized, clean lip videos, difficult visual conditions, extremely constrained edge devices, and lost articulatory detail. It also discusses the synthetic-to-natural speech gap through the Lombard effect and expands the proposed interpretation of VQ as a semantic anchor and regularizer.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents unshared encoder parameters, from-scratch retraining with frozen DP-LipCoder in Table 2, and which Table 3 baseline results were reproduced versus taken from papers. The reproducibility statement replaces its direct GitHub reference with the project homepage; an actual change in resource availability is not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for FMA (Defferrard et al., 2017) and FSD50K (Fonseca et al., 2022), supporting the new noise evaluations. The related-work sections and positioning against existing AVSS architectures remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes the Dolphin prefix from the title, updates affiliation and publication-header text, adds limitations and acknowledgments, and inserts three appendix sections. Clarifications and cross-references change locally, while the existing narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the VQ, four-panel noise, and MOS tables as Tables 7, 9, and 10. It enlarges Figure 4, expands Tables 2–3 captions, and relocates several displays. All nine scientific figures and the earlier tabular content are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its central discretization claim through comparisons that also differed architecturally, and its reported separation evaluations used artificial mixtures. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence with a controlled VQ ablation, systematic acoustic stress tests, and a blinded listening study on natural overlap. Explicit limitations and clearer experimental provenance further improve assessability. Undefined MOS ± values and unspecified noise-mixing levels still limit interpretation and reproducibility, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
